title: Buffering strategy and token-econ breakpoint analysis
summary: Working analysis that ties buffer sizing (reserve vs spot mix) to marginal $/1M token breakpoints across US, EU, APAC under different throughput and KV-cache scenarios. Goal: propose pragmatic sizing bands and a decision rule for when to convert spot capacity to reserved to hit unit-econ targets while preserving latency SLOs.
body:
Context:
This doc is a working playbook for how we think about short- and medium-term GPU capacity buffers and how that translates to token-level unit economics. We want a repeatable rule that ties: (1) forecast uncertainty (variance of demand spike), (2) spot/reserved mix, and (3) micro-architecture throughput (batching, KV cache hit) into a single breakpoint metric: $/1M tokens.

High-level goal:
- Provide simple decision boundaries (green/yellow/red) for on-call and capacity ops: at what utilization or regional price delta do we convert X% of spot to reserved or activate burst pools?
- Surface the marginal cost of serving 1M additional tokens per region so product and finance can compare to pricing tiers.

Assumptions (working, call out if you disagree):
- Model class: Gen-25B-ish family (moderate KV cache benefits). Per-GPU baseline throughput varies with batching and quantization.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (single active generation stream * average batch): conservative=50 t/s, baseline=100 t/s, aggressive=180 t/s.
- KV cache hit reduces average GPU compute by an effective multiplier on token generation: 0% hit -> 1.0x compute, 30% hit -> 0.75x, 60% hit -> 0.5x. This is a simplification but actionable.
- Regional effective GPU-hour costs (blended of on-prem/reserved/spot blended cost to Redwood; internal numbers):
  - US: reserved $4.00/hr, spot $1.90/hr
  - EU: reserved $4.80/hr, spot $2.10/hr
  - APAC: reserved $5.50/hr, spot $2.75/hr
- We express unit-econ as $ per 1M generated tokens (post-KV account).

Methodology (how to compute $/1M tokens):
1) tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600
2) effective_tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_hour * KV_multiplier (where KV_multiplier accounts for fewer GPU cycles spent on repeated prefixes — i.e., increases effective tokens per GPU-hour)
   - For clarity, KV_multiplier = 1 / compute_multiplier. If compute_multiplier=0.75, KV_multiplier=1.333 (you get 33% more effective tokens/hr)
3) cost_per_1M = gpu_hour_price / (effective_tokens_per_hour / 1e6)

Quick example (baseline = 100 t/s, 30% KV hit -> compute_multiplier=0.75 => KV_multiplier=1.333):
- tokens_per_hour = 100 * 3600 = 360,000 tokens/hr => 0.36M/hr
- effective_tokens_per_hour = 0.36M * 1.333 = 0.48M/hr
- US reserved $4.00/hr => cost_per_1M = 4.00 / 0.48 = $8.33 per 1M tokens
- US spot $1.90/hr => cost_per_1M = 1.90 / 0.48 = $3.96 per 1M tokens

Scenario matrix (conservative / baseline / aggressive) with KV hits (0%, 30%, 60%). The numbers below are rounded to two decimals.

Matrix explanation: rows are throughput scenarios (t/s), columns are regions/cost types. 

Throughput: 50 t/s (conservative)
- tokens/hr = 180,000 (0.18M)
  - KV 0% (mult=1.0 -> eff=0.18M/hr): US reserved $4.00 -> $22.22 /1M, US spot $1.90 -> $10.56 /1M
  - KV 30% (mult=0.75 -> eff=0.24M/hr): US reserved -> $16.67 /1M, US spot -> $7.92 /1M
  - KV 60% (mult=0.5 -> eff=0.36M/hr): US reserved -> $11.11 /1M, US spot -> $5.28 /1M

Throughput: 100 t/s (baseline)
- tokens/hr = 360,000 (0.36M)
  - KV 0% (eff=0.36M): US reserved -> $11.11 /1M, spot -> $5.28 /1M
  - KV 30% (eff=0.48M): US reserved -> $8.33 /1M, spot -> $3.96 /1M
  - KV 60% (eff=0.72M): US reserved -> $5.56 /1M, spot -> $2.64 /1M

Throughput: 180 t/s (aggressive)
- tokens/hr = 648,000 (0.648M)
  - KV 0% (eff=0.648M): US reserved -> $6.17 /1M, spot -> $2.93 /1M
  - KV 30% (eff=0.864M): US reserved -> $4.63 /1M, spot -> $2.20 /1M
  - KV 60% (eff=1.296M): US reserved -> $3.09 /1M, spot -> $1.46 /1M

Notes about EU / APAC numbers: same formula. Expect EU reserved costs to be ~20% higher than US reserved and spot ~10% higher than US spot in our blended inputs; APAC sits above that. For reference, baseline (100 t/s, 30% KV) yields: EU reserved ~ $10.00 /1M, APAC reserved ~ $11.46 /1M (rounded).

Interpreting breakpoints and decision rules:
- Baseline rule: target $/1M <= $10 for non-enterprise (default product tier). If regional reserved price leads to >$10 at baseline, we should either: (a) increase KV caching (prompt engineering, longer prefix retention), or (b) convert a portion of spot to reserved to guarantee capacity (if spot price is volatile), or (c) shift routing to cheaper region if latency allows.
- Spot-reserved mix rule: operate with a target blended cost and a buffer band. Example operating point: blended_cost_target = $6/1M, buffer band = +/- 20%. If spot+reserved mix pushes blended beyond 20% higher, trigger reserve conversions or activate burst.
- Latency SLO note: low-latency requests (P95 < 200ms) typically reduce batching and effective tokens/sec by 30–50%. For low-latency workloads, treat tokens/sec as conservative scenario when evaluating $/1M.

Buffer sizing / runway calculation (simple):
- Inputs: current daily tokens demand (D), forecasted growth rate r (daily), acceptable outage probability p, buffer_days b
- We compute required buffer GPUs = ceil( (peak_daily_tokens - committed_capacity_tokens) / tokens_per_gpu_per_day ) where peak_daily_tokens = D * (1 + safety_multiplier) and safety_multiplier derived from demand variance and p (e.g., p=0.95 -> safety_multiplier = +50% for heavy-tailed spikes).
- Example: daily tokens = 150M, committed reserved capacity = 300 GPU-hr/day (i.e., 300 * effective_tokens_per_hour), baseline effective tokens/hr (0.48M/hr in our sample) => one GPU provides 0.48M/hr * 24 = 11.52M/day -> 300 GPUs -> 3,456M/day capacity (sized big here). This highlights we must be careful mapping tokens/day to GPU-hours with proper KPIs.

Operational playbook (practical):
- Week-of: maintain a rolling 3-day spot buffer of X% (default 25%) to absorb bursts. If spot utilization > 70% of spot pool for two consecutive 1-hour windows AND blended $/1M projected > threshold, flag for reserve conversion (automated runbook).
- Monthly: re-evaluate blended regional costs vs. 90-day usage patterns. If a region shows consistently >2x spot volatility, increase reserved fraction for the SLAs that need it.
- Emergency: if predicted blended $/1M > 1.5x target and demand growth > 20% week-over-week, trigger manual on-call to approve one-time reserved ramp or cross-region shift.

Example decision thresholds (nominal):
- Green: blended $/1M <= $7 -> no changes, operate with 20% spot buffer
- Yellow: $7 < blended <= $12 -> investigate, consider increasing KV retention, check routing, prepare reserve conversion plan
- Red: blended > $12 -> convert up to 50% of spot capacity to reserved for critical SLA classes, or throttle non-critical workloads

Open questions / risk items:
- Our blended GPU-hour costs are noisy; we need to replace assumptions with actual billing + amortized on-prem if available (ENGINF-4123 ticket tracking).
- KV multiplier is model- and prompt-dependent; we should instrument more production routes to measure realized compute reduction per prefix hit.
- We assume tokens/sec is stable per GPU. In reality, multi-tenant concurrency, continuous batching, and request shape skew will change realized throughput. Need SRE experiment.

Recommendations (next short steps):
1) Run a 2-week A/B experiment on a non-critical region: enforce aggressive KV retention (increase prefix window) on 10% of traffic and measure delta in tokens_per_gpu_hour (ticket: ENGINF-4198).
2) Add blended $/1M metric to Redwood Console per route (product) and a region-level panel with green/yellow/red thresholds.
3) Pilot automation: implement a conservative runbook that flips 10% of spot -> reserved automatically when blended $/1M enters red for >1 hour (manual approval gate currently required).

Appendix: quick conversion formulas (copyable)
- tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- effective_tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_hour / compute_multiplier  # compute_multiplier = fraction of full compute compared to no-KV
- cost_per_1M = gpu_hour_price / (effective_tokens_per_hour / 1e6)

Checklist before formalizing into a spreadsheet:
- [ ] Replace blended region costs with actual billing numbers (last 90 days)
- [ ] Run in-prod measurement for tokens_per_gpu_hour across 10 routes (low-latency, mid, batch)
- [ ] Instrument runtime to report 'effective_tokens_per_hour' per GPU pool hourly
- [ ] Draft automation policy for spot->reserved conversion and sign-off with finance

Document history and author notes:
- v0.1 (2024-01-18) initial draft by Sophia Chen
- v0.2 (2024-02-05) added scenario matrix and decision thresholds (Ravi Patel)
- v0.3 (2024-03-05) clarified KV multiplier and operational playbook (Ava Martinez)

End of doc. Please add experimental results and adjusted regional prices as comments below so we can bake into the next pass.
